question_stem:
Oxygen-15 ($^{15}_{8}\text{O}$) is radioactive and has a half-life of 2.04 minutes.

The decay of oxygen-15 produces positrons. For this reason, oxygen-15 is sometimes used as a tracer in positron emission tomography (PET scanning).

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by a tracer.

parts.label: (b)
parts.part_stem: The equation for the decay of oxygen-15 is $$^{15}_{8}\text{O} \rightarrow ^{P}_{Q}\text{X} + ^{R}_{S}\beta^{+} + Z$$ where X is the nucleus formed during the decay and Z is another particle.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: State the values of the integers $P$, $Q$, $R$ and $S$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State the name of particle Z.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Define the activity of a sample.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate the decay constant of oxygen-15. Give a unit with your answer.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the rate at which positrons are produced in a sample of oxygen-15 that has a mass of $2.85 \times 10^{-6} \text{kg}$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.part_stem: The particles that are emitted from the body and detected outside it during PET scanning are not positrons but another type of particle.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: State the name of the particles that are detected.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: Explain how these particles are formed inside the body.
